headline: COPPER ENTERS BEAR MARKET, WORST WEEK OF 2026 — $186B Wiped From 11 Largest Producers; Druckenmiller Goes Short
snippet: LME copper has entered bear market territory after falling 18% from its September 2026 peak, with Thursday marking the metal's worst weekly performance since November 2022, and $186 billion in market cap erased from the 11 largest copper-exposed miners over a single month. Stan Druckenmiller disclosed a copper short position, Mercuria's metals research head described end-user demand as 'closer to recessionary than growth,' and simultaneous selloffs across AI-infrastructure equity and industrial metals signals that speculative AI-demand bets driving copper to record mid-2026 levels are being rapidly unwound — leaving Teck, Antofagasta, First Quantum and Lundin all sharply lower on the week.

headline: ENDEAVOUR SILVER PITARRILLA FEASIBILITY DELIVERS $736M NPV — 4,000 tpd Underground Mine in Durango Ready for Build Decision
snippet: Endeavour Silver (NYSE/TSX: EXK) completed its Feasibility Study for the Pitarrilla silver project in Durango, Mexico on November 19, delivering an after-tax NPV of US$736 million on a 4,000-tonne-per-day mechanized underground mine targeting the high-grade sulphide core of one of Mexico's largest undeveloped silver deposits. The study represents a construction-ready project profile at a time when silver's structural supply deficit — now entering its sixth consecutive year — provides a compelling long-term demand argument for primary silver producers willing to bring new supply to market despite current price headwinds; a NI 43-101 technical report is to be filed within 45 days.

headline: SNOWLINE DRILLS 450M AT 1.47 g/t AU AND CONFIRMS SECOND GOLD SYSTEM AT DUKE — Two Large Targets on Rogue, Yukon
snippet: Snowline Gold (TSX-V: SGD) released drill results confirming 1.47 g/t gold over 450.2 metres from surface at the Valley deposit on its Rogue Project in Yukon — the longest continuous gold interval yet reported at Valley — alongside first results from the new Duke target 12 kilometres to the southeast, which cut 1.03 g/t gold over 65.8 metres and establishes a reduced intrusion-related gold system distinct from Valley's style of mineralization. The confirmation that the Rogue property hosts at least two large-scale gold systems separated by 12 kilometres of largely unexplored ground significantly expands the project's prospective footprint.

headline: MIDNIGHT SUN EXPANDS ZAMBIA COPPER SYSTEM TO 12.1km — Northern Block Drilling Grows Discovery Zone
snippet: Midnight Sun Mining (TSX-V: MMA) released assay results from 10 additional diamond drill holes confirming and expanding higher-grade copper mineralization across the Northern Block of its Dumbwa discovery in Zambia's Copperbelt region, extending the total established near-surface copper system to 12.1 kilometres of strike length — nearly double the 6.7 kilometres confirmed as recently as mid-2026. With five rigs still active and an initial resource estimate now within reach as the mineralized footprint approaches its Phase One extent, Dumbwa ranks among the most active large-scale copper exploration campaigns underway globally.

headline: YUKON METALS HITS 10.41% COPPER AND 6.27 g/t GOLD ON SURFACE AT AZ — New Porphyry Zones in Western Yukon
snippet: Yukon Metals (CSE: YMC) reported surface rock samples grading up to 10.41% copper and 6.27 g/t gold from multiple new zones at its AZ copper-gold project in western Yukon, with the results identifying porphyry-style targets distinct from previously known vein-hosted mineralization and informing the positioning of the first 2026 drill hole AZ26-007, results of which are pending. At 13,110 hectares located 36 kilometres south of Beaver Creek along the Alaska Highway corridor, AZ sits in one of Yukon's least-drilled yet historically high-grade copper-gold districts.

headline: USAR CHAIRMAN BETS $3M ON COMPANY AFTER 40% YTD SLIDE — Insider Signal As Policy Tailwinds Meet Operational Uncertainty
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) chairman Michael Blitzer purchased approximately $3 million in company stock across three transactions this week — one of the largest insider purchases since the company's 2025 public listing — as the stock sat more than 40% below its year-to-date high following the William Blair downgrade that cited processing capacity uncertainties. The insider buy follows a week in which USAR shares recovered sharply on President Trump's rare earth pledge and US-China bilateral talks, but remained deeply depressed on a year-to-date basis; Blitzer's $3 million personal commitment adds a conviction signal from someone with direct access to project-level operational data.

headline: SILVER FACES 35MOz DEFICIT IN 2026 — Sixth Consecutive Year of Undersupply; 762MOz Cumulative Drawdown Since 2021
snippet: The Silver Institute's 2026 mid-year update confirms the silver market is on track for a 35-million-ounce supply deficit this year — the sixth consecutive annual shortfall — even as prices fell sharply, with total 2026 demand projected at 1.08 billion ounces while mining supply and recycling fall short by 35Moz; cumulative stock drawdowns since 2021 have reached 762 million ounces. The persistence of structural undersupply through a year in which silver prices fell nearly 30% from their January all-time high above $100 per ounce creates an increasingly stretched physical market backdrop for 2027, when solar photovoltaic and electrification demand is projected to accelerate.

headline: BLUE MOON METALS CLOSES $36.7M TURNER COPPER-GOLD IN OREGON — Hub-and-Spoke Critical Minerals Model Expands
snippet: Blue Moon Metals (TSX-V: MOON / Nasdaq: BMM) completed its acquisition of the Turner copper-gold volcanic massive sulphide deposit in O'Brien, Oregon on November 19, paying $4.7 million cash plus approximately 4.78 million shares plus $7 million in milestones for total consideration of roughly US$36.7 million — adding a third VMS deposit to its Western US Critical Minerals Hub strategy alongside the Blue Moon Mine in California and the Springer complex in Nevada. Turner is a past-producing underground VMS mine with a 1.5% NSR; Blue Moon plans to integrate it with its Nevada mill hub model for a consolidated critical minerals processing operation.

headline: FREEPORT EXPANDS ITS TOODOGGONE BC COPPER STAKE — Major Consolidating Ground as $110M CAD Aurora West Deal Takes Shape
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan is consolidating its position in the Toodoggone copper-gold district of northern British Columbia following its C$110 million acquisition of a 51% stake in TDG Gold's Aurora West project, with North of 60 Mining News reporting on November 20 that Freeport is actively expanding ground in the district as one of several majors building positions in BC's copper belt. The Aurora West deal includes earn-in provisions allowing Freeport to increase its stake to 75% by spending C$80 million on exploration and paying C$40 million, positioning the company to convert the Toodoggone's known copper-gold endowment into a potential major mine development in one of North America's most prospective copper jurisdictions.

headline: CNBC: GOLD'S BAD YEAR IS GETTING WORSE — Rate-Dollar Spiral Driving 14-Month Lows; December FOMC Is the Pivot Test
snippet: CNBC's November 19 analysis of gold's prolonged 2026 decline — now 29% from January's all-time high above $5,500 per ounce and sitting at a 14-month low — identifies rising real Treasury yields and a strengthening US dollar as the primary mechanisms suppressing precious metals, with 90%-plus market probability for a December Fed rate hike eliminating the near-term catalyst that could stabilize the correction. The piece distinguishes between the financial conditions driving the selloff and the structural demand factors that remain intact — central bank buying, geopolitical risk premium, de-dollarization thesis — framing the December FOMC meeting as the key inflection point that could either confirm further downside or mark the correction low.
